search_files confirms these tokens occur only in code-review-verify.md prose and verify_models.py `description=` strings — no parser/branch reads them; the LLM verifier is the sole consumer, which the Rule-5 guard classifies as NOT a non-human consumer, so these prose greps guard wording rather than a parseable contract.

The actual gating BEHAVIOR (managed removal never boosts; unmanaged boosts to serious) is already covered behaviorally in tests/unit/test_impact_code.py:426-441, so removing the prose-token asserts loses no regression coverage.
advisory.finding: test_unversioned_break_is_version_signal_gated_on_both_surfaces and test_verify_prompt_keys_removed_public_symbol_on_export assert on prose-wording tokens in the prompt .md prose and the Pydantic `description=` metadata ('major version bump', 'deprecation cycle', 'CHANGELOG breaking-change', 'managed', 'does not prove', 'CLI command', 'MCP tool'). These tokens are consumed only by the LLM verifier (not a non-human parser — no code branches on them), so the assertions are change-detectors that break on a behavior-preserving reword of the prompt/description without any observable-behavior change. The field-NAME and `.default is False` checks in the same tests are valid contract assertions (decide.impact_code reads those exact identifiers) and should be kept.
scenarios: A future edit rewords the prompt bullet or field description (e.g. 'major version bump' -> 'a bump of the major version') while preserving the LLM-observable contract; these tests fail spuriously.
